# Types of advertising and how to use them

Spotify Editorial Team

Share This

## **Just getting to grips with digital marketing? Don't feel so daunted—in this guide we'll walk you through the different types of digital advertising and help you determine the right path for marketing your business. We'll also take a look at the types of advertisements available to you on Spotify.**

Trying to find the best advertising strategy can feel like a wild goose chase. What works for one brand may not work for another, which means you can’t rely solely on what others tell you. What you can do, though, is study the different types of advertising and get to know the unique pros and cons associated with each.

A little education goes a long way. You’ll feel better prepared to make informed choices about which advertising methods best fit your business. You know your customers best, and you are the best person to make the final call on what types of ads your brand should invest in.

Let’s take a closer look at your options and the benefits they offer.

## The 3 core types of advertising

There are three high-level advertising types that serve as the pillars of promotional marketing. Each of these is far-reaching, with several sub-categories.

### Print advertising

The oldest advertising method which anyone reading this will be familiar with—but by no means the least profitable. Print advertising encompasses all printed materials that are created and distributed for the purposes of connecting with a target audience, and can attract lots of new customers. A few of the most popular forms of print advertising include magazine ads, billboards, direct mail (including flyers, catalogs, and postcards).

### Broadcast advertising

Broadcast advertising refers to ads delivered during television and radio broadcasts. The most common broadcast ads include:

##### Radio ads

Radio ads are audio-only adverts that are aired during or in-between scheduled radio broadcasts. They’re great for building brand awareness and more cost-effective than other forms of advertising—but they often lack personalization since listeners don’t share personal information with radio stations, and engagement metrics are very difficult to measure.

##### TV ads

TV ads air on broadcast, satellite, or closed-circuit television channels, and are ideal for brands looking to raise awareness with a wide audience. The widely known downside, however, is that they carry a high price tag if you want your ad to air during prime-time slots or on national television.

##### Pre-movie ads

Pre-movie ads are shown in movie theaters prior to a film being shown. These ads aren’t shown in just one theater, but in multiple theaters across a particular franchise. They allow advertisers to connect with an audience that’s already captivated in an environment where there are few distractions, but pre-movie ads can be costly to run.

### Digital advertising

Digital advertising is an umbrella term for any form of paid marketing that occurs via online channels like social media, websites, search engines, streaming services, and so on. Popular types of digital ads include:

##### Pay-per-click ads

Pay-per-click ads, or PPC ads, are displayed in search engine results pages like Google and Bing. A business pays each time a user clicks on its ad—and the cost depends on the competitiveness of the keyword the ad is targeting. For businesses who want to advertise niche products that don’t get high search volumes, the cost might be quite low. However, for businesses competing in crowded markets the cost may be quite high. Either way, PPC ads are highly trackable and—if you don’t want to play the long game—a shortcut to the top of search engine results pages (SERPs).

##### Social media ads

Any paid advertisement that’s displayed on a social media platform like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, or LinkedIn falls into this category. A social media ad is an excellent option in terms of being able to target your desired audience based on their interests and other key demographics such as age and location, but it’s often hard to calculate ROI as conversion rates can be impacted by a long list of factors not known by the platform.

##### Video & audio ads

Digital audio is the fastest growing form of advertising1 and—as of 2022—87% of marketers claim videos have a positive ROI2. Audio ads combine the wide reach and scalability of traditional radio with the fine-tuned targeting abilities of digital media. With Spotify, digital audio ads are served during [podcasts](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/ad-experiences/podcast-ads/), and music playlists.

## The power of Spotify ads

Sure, we’re known for our extensive library of music and podcasts, but that’s not what defines us at Spotify. What truly sets us apart and gives us our competitive edge is the trust placed in us by more than [450 million global users](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/news-and-insights/spotify-third-quarter-earnings-2022/) who actively consume content on our platform each month.

It’s because of our listeners that our app is available in 183 different markets. It’s also because of them we’ve earned the title of the top global audio streaming service3. As much as we work to offer an audio experience our users will love, it’s their commitment to our platform that fuels our progress, and it’s what makes Spotify such a force to be reckoned with when it comes to [advertising for small businesses.](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/small-business-advertising/)

To be exact, [59% of our users](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/news-and-insights/digital-audio-kantar-2021/) say they pay more attention to ads on Spotify than on traditional radio, and Spotify ads have been proven to [drive higher engagement levels](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/news-and-insights/sonic-science/) than all other forms of media.

Here are the different types of advertising formats available to you through Spotify:

#### 1\. Audio ads

Of all the types of advertisement formats we provide, [audio ads](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/ad-experiences/audio-ads/) continue to be the most popular, and for good reason. Our advanced [audience targeting capabilities](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/audience-targeting/) enable advertisers to reach the right people, in the right place, at the right moment. Plus, audio ads can’t be closed or swiped past, ensuring your message is heard and your campaign is given the greatest chance of success. You can choose between a 15-second or 30-second ad slot, and we provide a full range of [self-serve tools and services](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/creating-audio-ads/) to help you create audio ads that your audience will love.

#### 2\. Display ads

# Should Your Business Use Spotify Ads?

Daphne Keng

October 7, 2024

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69f5004787578f925928360d/6a50ff6f06e1fcbf958855ae_67030cba99faa148651deb2c_Depositphotos_497187120_L%2520\(1\).jpeg)

Digital Advertising

Wondering if Spotify ads could be the right move for [your business](https://www.yourdigitalresource.com/blog-categories/entrepreneurship)? It's a fair question, considering Spotify has grown into a global audio streaming powerhouse with millions of listeners tuning in daily.  

Whether you run a cozy coffee shop with indie vibes or a booming online store, Spotify might just be the place to flex your advertising muscles. From boosting brand awareness to skyrocketing your sales, the platform can work wonders for your business.

But here’s the catch: not every marketing channel suits every business. While Spotify could offer the perfect audience for your next campaign, it's important to consider whether it aligns with your business goals and target audience.

Is Spotify really the right stage for your brand? How do you make sure your ad doesn’t just blend into background noise? Our SEO company in Dallas will unpack these questions and more, giving you a clear picture of what Spotify ads can do for you.  

Ready to see if these ads could be your brand’s next big hit? Let’s hit play and find out!

## What’s the Deal with Spotify Ads?

Before we dive into to the deeper details, let’s quickly tune into what Spotify ads actually are. More than just a massive library of music and [podcasts](https://www.yourdigitalresource.com/post/optimize-podcast-for-maximum-listenership), these ads act as a stage for businesses to connect with potential customers, allowing you to weave your message into the listening experience of millions worldwide.  

Whether it’s through short, snappy audio clips that play between songs, visually engaging banners that pop up in the app, or interactive video spots during a music break, Spotify gives your brand a voice (and sometimes a face) in a very personal, direct way. It’s all about catching the vibe of your audience right where they are – deep in their music journey.  

### The Pros and Cons  

As mentioned earlier by your [trusted SEO company](https://www.yourdigitalresource.com/local-marketing/dallas-seo-company) in Dallas, not every marketing channel works for just about any business. Let’s explore its ups and downs to see if Spotify can harmonize with your goals.

#### Pros:

##### 1\. Targeted Reach

One of Spotify's killer features is its deep dive into user data. You can target ads based on age, gender, location, interests, and even music tastes. Imagine your ad hitting the ears of jazz lovers or workout warriors. The platform makes it possible!

This precise targeting helps make sure your ads land with the right crowd, rather than just throwing them into the wind and hoping for the best.

##### 2\. Engaged Listeners

![woman happily listening with her headphones](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69f5004787578f925928360d/6a50ff6f06e1fcbf95885597_67030d9ed0cd6c8a1d11fa15_67030d37062624eb347d026c_Depositphotos_365148740_L%252520\(1\).jpeg)

Unlike visual media where ads can often be overlooked, audio ads capture the undivided attention of listeners. Spotify users typically engage through headphones, which provides a unique one-on-one scenario. This means your message is delivered in a personal, direct manner, potentially increasing the impact of your message.

##### 3\. Flexible Formats

Spotify isn’t one-note when it comes to ads. Choose from audio clips that fit between songs, eye-catching video ads during browsing, or even branded playlists. This lets you play around and find the best way to connect with your audience, be it a quick hello or a deeper engagement.

##### 4\. Safety First

Another reason that makes Spotify great is that it’s a brand-safe zone. You don't have to worry about your ad popping up next to some iffy content. The platform makes sure your ad only hangs out in good company, which is super crucial for keeping your reputation flawless.

##### 5\. Innovative Engagement Opportunities

With Spotify, there's room to really get creative. We’re talking about [Sponsored Sessions](https://ads.spotify.com/en-US/ad-experiences/sponsored-sessions-specs/) where listeners get ad-free music for a bit thanks to you, or Playlist Takeovers where your brand curates the tunes. Not only do these features enhance user experience, but they also increase the time your audience spends with your brand, leading to deeper engagement.

#### Cons:

##### 1\. Limited Visibility

The experts at our SEO company in Dallas agree that audio ads are fantastic. However, they don’t have a visual element – unless you opt for video, which only shows when the app is in use. If your product needs to be seen to spark interest, this might dampen the impact of audio-only spots.

##### 2\. Skip Rates

One of the challenges with Spotify ads is the ability for users to skip audio ads after a few seconds. This means your ad needs to grab attention and engage listeners almost immediately. If it doesn’t hook your audience right away, you might miss the chance to convey your full message.

##### 3\. Money-Draining

![stressed man in front of a blackboard with a thought bubble containing dollar sign ](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69f5004787578f925928360d/6a50ff6f06e1fcbf95885594_6703235468332b323b065d70_67032259b7ff44f45597d5de_Depositphotos_338522158_L%252520\(1\).jpeg)

While Spotify offers various pricing levels, launching a comprehensive ad campaign can be pricey, especially for smaller businesses. The cost can be a barrier for those with limited marketing budgets or those just testing the waters in audio advertising.

##### 4\. Tricky ROI

Title: Google Ads Benchmarks for YOUR Industry [Updated!]

URL Source: https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2016/02/29/google-adwords-industry-benchmarks

Published Time: 2016-02-19T05:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Whether you’re doing PPC for the first time or you’ve just signed a new client, it can be daunting to know whether or not you’re doing a good job. Sure, we all want to create unicorn ads that have [highest CTRs](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2014/02/11/average-click-through-rate) and the [best conversion rates](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2014/03/17/what-is-a-good-conversion-rate), but what’s a good metric for one industry isn’t necessarily good for another. So what numbers should you be looking to beat in your industry?

Check out the Google Ads industry benchmarks our clients are seeing, including:

*   Average click-through rate (CTR)
*   Average cost per click (CPC)
*   Average conversion rate (CVR)
*   Average cost per action (CPA)

You’ll find averages across these ads metrics for twenty industries: Advocacy, Auto, B2B, Consumer Services, Dating & Personals, E-Commerce, Education, Employment Services, Finance & Insurance, Health & Medical, Home Goods, Industrial Services, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, and Travel & Hospitality.

**![Image 1: ✴️](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/2734.svg) Note:**We update this data regularly! **[Download the PDF of our latest Google Ads Benchmarks report here](https://www.wordstream.com/resources/google-ads-industry-benchmarks?cid=Web_WS_InContent_Guide_GoogleAdsBenchmarks_Download&itm_source=wordstream&itm_medium=blog&itm_campaign=incontent_links).**

## Average Click-Through Rate in Google Ads by Industry

![Image 2: average ctr in adwords](https://www.wordstream.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/adwords-industry-benchmarks-average-ctr-3.png)

Dating and personal services really _click_ with PPC – boasting an average search CTR of 6%! No doubt, it’s easy to [write powerful emotional ad copy](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/11/09/emotional-ads) when your prospects are searching for love. Other industries with high search CTRs include Advocacy, Autos, and Travel.

When we first collected this data in 2015, legal services could struggle to attract attention on the SERP (with a relatively low average 1.35% CTR) – in large part due to [advertising restrictions](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2014/11/25/adwords-ad-disapproved) enforced by both Google and government organizations. [Legal advertisers](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/06/29/law-firm-marketing) have improved their stats in the past few years!

As of 2018, the industries with the lowest average click-through rates including Technology, B2B, and Consumer Services.

**The average click-through rate in Google Ads across all industries is 3.17% for search and 0.46% for display.**

Both of these averages are higher than they were a couple of years ago: Good news for Ads advertisers and agencies!

### Average Click Through Rate (CTR)

| Industry | Average CTR (Search) | Average CTR (GDN) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Advocacy | 4.41% | 0.59% |
| Auto | 4.00% | 0.60% |
| B2B | 2.41% | 0.46% |
| Consumer Services | 2.41% | 0.51% |
| Dating & Personals | 6.05% | 0.72% |
| E-Commerce | 2.69% | 0.51% |
| Education | 3.78% | 0.53% |
| Employment Services | 2.42% | 0.59% |
| Finance & Insurance | 2.91% | 0.52% |
| Health & Medical | 3.27% | 0.59% |
| Home Goods | 2.44% | 0.49% |
| Industrial Services | 2.61% | 0.50% |
| Legal | 2.93% | 0.59% |
| Real Estate | 3.71% | 1.08% |
| Technology | 2.09% | 0.39% |
| Travel & Hospitality | 4.68% | 0.47% |

![Image 3: 📙](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f4d9.svg)**Free guide [>> Hacking Google Ads: One Trick That Could Save You Thousands](https://marketing.wordstream.com/WSLIQContentDLWebsiteHackingGoogleAds.html?cid=Web_Any_BlogInContent_PPC_HackingGoogleAds_Download)**

## Average Cost Per Click in Google Ads by Industry

![Image 4: contextual display costs](https://www.wordstream.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/adwords-industry-benchmarks-average-cpc-5.png)

It’s no surprise that legal services have some of the highest CPCs among all Google ads on the search network. Both “Lawyer” and “Attorney” make the top 10 [most expensive keywords on Google](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2011/07/18/most-expensive-keywords-google-adwords) and [on Bing](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/03/19/most-expensive-keywords-bing-ads). Average CPCs in the legal industry are over $6. Consumer services aren’t too far behind, with an average CPC of $6.40.

Advocacy and nonprofit groups are fortunate to have a cost per click under $2, likely as a result of the $2 max CPC bid [Google Grant advertisers](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2013/12/18/google-grants-adwords-for-nonprofits) have to set on all of their [keywords](https://www.wordstream.com/keywords).

Most industries have pretty inexpensive CPCs on the Google Display Network. The only industry with costs per click over $1 on the Display network is Dating & Personals.

**The average cost per click in Google Ads across all industries is $2.69 for search and $0.63 for display.**

The news here is good too: These [Google Ads costs](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/05/21/how-much-does-adwords-cost) have increased very little over the figures we found a couple of years ago (when the averages were $2.32 and $0.58 respectively).

## Average Conversion Rates in Google Ads by Industry

![Image 5: average conversion rate in adwords](https://www.wordstream.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/adwords-industry-benchmarks-average-conversion-rate-2.png)

A couple of years ago, the Finance and Insurance industries were leading the pack when it came to conversion rates.

However, our newly updated data shows that the Dating & Personal industry is way out ahead now, with search conversion rates on average over 9%! Other standouts include the legal industries, consumer services, and autos.

Title: About Display ads and the Google Display Network

URL Source: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190

Markdown Content:
We’re bringing the flexibility of standard Display campaigns and the AI capabilities of Smart Display campaigns into a single Display campaign. In addition to the existing benefits of Smart Display campaigns, you now have the ability to choose the level of AI integration that you prefer for bidding, creatives, and targeting.

Smart Display campaigns have been integrated into the standard Display campaign offering, enhancing them with AI-powered features. Any existing Smart Display campaigns in your account will have migrated to this unified Display campaign structure without any action needed on your part. This migration shouldn't cause any fluctuations in your campaign's performance. If you're looking to create a Smart campaign and can no longer find that option, this updated Display campaign is the successor, offering similar AI capabilities with more control. For other automated campaign types, consider Performance Max or Search campaigns. Learn more [About (newly simplified) Display campaigns](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/12035738).

![Image 1](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/sPzwT-Bqx1aPfz50W-D45GUr80uja1sxUU18uBPhSZpE7GsSzl07WUqSSyU1z-0mvE8=w150)[Display campaigns](https://support.google.com/google-ads/topic/10016807) serve visually engaging ads on the Google Display Network. The Display Network helps you reach people as they browse millions of websites, apps, and Google-owned properties (such as YouTube and Gmail).

Display campaigns offer a simple, intelligent solution to managing the complex variables of display advertising, and may be the most effortless way to broaden your customer base and win new conversions. Use a Display campaign to show ads in almost all formats across the Google Display Network, reaching people at all stages in the buying cycle—from people with demonstrated interests to customers just about to buy.

**On this page**

*   [Benefits](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#Benefits)
*   [How the Google Display Network works](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#How-the-Google-Display-Network-works)
*   [Get started on Responsive display ads](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#Get-started-on-Responsive-display-ads)
*   [How Display ads work](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#How-Display-ads-work)
*   [Keep in mind the Google Display Network timeline](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#Keep-in-mind-the-Google-Display-Network-timeline)

## [Benefits](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190)

*   **Reach people in multiple places**: Display campaigns can reach people worldwide across 35 million websites and apps, and on Google-owned properties (YouTube and Gmail). This allows you to expand your reach beyond just Google Search.
*   **Build campaigns around your goals**: Drive sales, leads, and website traffic or build awareness and consideration for your business, product, or service.
*   **Designed for ease of use**: Display campaigns use AI-powered solutions across targeting, bidding, and formats to reach a new or existing audience. This can help your campaign deliver the best campaign results, friction-free. 
    *   **Optimized targeting**: Find the best performing audience segments that include potential customers with the highest likelihood to help you meet your conversion goals. [Learn more about optimized targeting](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10537509)
    *   **Smart bidding**: Bidding that uses AI to optimize for conversions or conversion value in each and every auction. It helps you save time and improve performance. [Learn more about Smart bidding](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7065882)

*   **A top-performing campaign in minutes**: You enter the building blocks for your ads—like headlines, images, and logos—and we’ll find you as many customers as we can within the CPA bid and budget you control.
*   **Smarter, not harder**: Display campaigns optimize within days. Google AI selects the best combination of assets to give your campaign the best performance. In this way, you can learn which of your headlines, descriptions, images, and logos perform best.

## [How the Google Display Network works](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190)

The Google Display Network helps you find the right audience with its targeting options that strategically show your message to potential customers at the right place and the right time. Display campaigns include AI capabilities that help improve campaign performance:

*   **Bidding**: [Smart Bidding strategies](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7065882) will be recommended to you based on your advertising goals. You can, however, choose not to use the suggested bidding strategies, and can manually select your bidding strategies. 
    *   **Pay for conversions**: You can pay for conversions, instead of clicks on Display campaigns that use Target CPA bidding. When setting up your campaign, go to the “Bidding” section. Look for the header labeled “Pay for” and select Conversions from the dropdown menu. Learn more [about pay for conversions](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7528254).

*   **Creatives**: By default, your [Display ads are responsive](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6363750) (unless you’re using uploaded Display ads). That means that you can upload different assets into Google Ads, and Google AI will determine the optimal combination of assets as well as the optimal size, appearance, and format of assets to fit available ad spaces with an ad format that is most likely to perform well.
*   **Targeting**: [Optimized targeting](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10537509) uses information such as keywords on your landing page to help you reach new and relevant audiences that are likely to convert. Optimized targeting is set as the default targeting method for your Display campaigns. If you prefer not to use optimized targeting, you can select a different form of targeting.

#### Optimize your campaign as you create it

As you create your campaign, you may receive notifications based on your setting selections. These notifications may alert you of issues that can result in decreased performance or that may be significant enough to prevent you from publishing your campaign.

The campaign construction navigation menu that appears as you construct your campaign provides a holistic view of your construction progress and will call attention to notifications that you may want to address. Move between steps in the navigation menu to easily review and resolve potential issues with your targeting, bidding, budget, or other campaign settings. Learn how to [Set up your campaign for success](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9451609).
